A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same latent-learning and episodic-retrieval study. Their complete text, equations, figures, table, and Appendices A-C support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on codebooks, simple reversals, semantic structure, and gridworld navigation with behavioral cloning and reinforcement learning, plus appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds a training-map-count ablation for gridworld reinforcement learning in Appendix C.3.

M1.justification: Sections 5 and B.3 retain the transformer architectures, supervised objectives, IMPALA with reconstruction losses, and oracle-retrieval procedures. The added training-map-count condition changes an experimental setting, not the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same codebooks, simple reversals, semantic-structure variants, and pixel-based RL and ASCII-based BC gridworld tasks. The added 100-map RL ablation changes sample count within retained coverage.

E2.justification: The baseline and oracle-retrieval comparisons and existing ablation variants remain. The new fewer-maps condition ablates the existing retrieval model's training setting rather than introducing another comparison method. Added literature citations are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: New Appendix C.3 evaluates gridworld RL with 100 training maps, compared with 3,072 in the retained main RL experiment. This adds a sample-size control motivated by the existing 100-map BC setting; it does not replace the main protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 and Figure 10 add an ablation asking whether RL retrieval still generalizes with fewer training maps. Existing ICL, batch-size, irrelevant-retrieval, and sequence-length analyses remain; v1's Appendix C.3 becomes C.4.

E5.justification: Figures 3-4 retain 95% confidence intervals across four runs. Figure 6 retains binomial intervals for BC and bootstrap intervals across three runs for RL. Figure 7(c)'s error-bar values change, but no changed run count or uncertainty-estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: New Figure 10 reports high trained-object success but near-zero latent-object success for retrieval trained on 100 RL maps. Figure 7(c) also slightly lowers the reported no-ICL retrieval validation score and raises its near-zero latent-test score, with revised error bars. Other retained result graphics are unchanged; Figure 1(d) redisplays existing simple-reversal results.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains the same input/task/output formalization, non-injectivity reasoning, and reversal examples. No mathematical definition, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract now explicitly attributes the weakness to parametric machine-learning systems. Section 7 replaces 'potentially novel perspective' with 'different perspective,' tempering novelty positioning. The five stated contributions and central oracle-retrieval and ICL claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 7 expands the distinction between online replay for prediction and decision-making and offline replay for consolidation and generalization. New Appendix C.3 interprets the map-count result as differing RL/BC generalization requirements, while explicitly leaving loss-related versus representation-related explanations unresolved.

D1.justification: Appendix B and Table 1 retain the architecture, optimization, tokenization, retrieval filtering, cached-memory implementation, and hyperparameter disclosures. No code/data access information or additional implementation instructions accompany the new sample-size ablation.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted references on hippocampal generalization, imagination, online/offline replay, semantic cognition, and RL retrieval, including Eichenbaum and Fortin, Eldar et al., and Humphreys et al. It removes the Teyler and DiScenna memory-index citation and broadens that framing toward generalization, while retaining the main research positioning.

P1.justification: There are targeted abstract, introduction, background, and discussion edits, an added Stanford affiliation, and an expanded online/offline replay discussion. The overall organization remains, with one new appendix subsection and consequential renumbering.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is rearranged to accommodate a fourth panel illustrating existing reversal results, with an expanded caption. A new map-count plot becomes Figure 10; the existing BC ablation moves and becomes Figure 11. The remaining displays retain their structure apart from local reflow.

improvement.justification: The new map-count ablation provides a useful control on RL/BC differences and identifies a condition where retrieval fails despite strong trained-object performance. More precise claim wording and expanded replay discussion improve interpretation. These are limited gains: the main evidence remains largely stable, and both effective non-oracle retrieval and the causes of the RL/BC differences remain unresolved.
